content: Is anyone using Lean on Github Codespaces or another cloud based computing environment? How does it work? Are there instructions for using Lean in one?

I am trying to use the Lean package that comes with How To Prove It with Lean in codespaces. This worked several months ago, but doesn't anymore. I updated .devcontainer/devcontainer.json and .devcontainer.Dockerfile to what is recommended in #34615, and now I have a very strange problem. The information that is supposed to be in the InfoView is instead being displayed on top of the Lean file:

Anyone know what's going on and how to fix it?
Update: I tried deleting the Codespace and building it again, and now it doesn't work at all. I can see the list of files in the project, but I can't open any of them--even the README.md file.
It's not just How To Prove It with Lean. I just tried opening Mathematics in Lean in Codespaces (using the "Open in GitHub Codespaces" button here) and that didn't work either.
@Jeremy Avigad I remember you tried this at ICERM, what was the conclusion?
That's strange. I tried it at ICERM and it seemed to work (though I had to wait a long time). I'll try it again now.
@Jeremy Avigad Did it work? I tried again to open MIL in Codespaces, and it still doesn't work for me.

Sorry, while it was running, I starting doing something else, and then forgot about it entirely.

I just tried it again, and it worked for me. It's slow; it took at least 7 minutes to start, and then when I opened a file, it took another couple of minutes for the yellow bars to go away. But otherwise, it seems fine.

I think I figured it out. My web browser was the problem. I'm using a mac. In Safari, Codespaces doesn't work, but in Chrome it does. It used to work in Safari, so something must have changed. I'm going to add something to the preface of How To Prove It with Lean saying that Codespaces doesn't work in all web browsers, and if you have trouble you should try switching browsers.

By the way, the file mathlib4/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json includes the lines:

  "hostRequirements": {
    "cpus": 4,
    "memory": "8gb"
  },

Those lines are not in the devcontainer.json file for MIL, so when I opened MIL in Codespaces, the default was for a 2-core machine. There is a pop-up menu offering a choice between 2 cores (8GB RAM) and 4 cores (16GB RAM), and I found that it made a big difference to switch to the 4-core option. So you might want to add the specification of 4 cpus to your devcontainer.json file. (My guess is that the memory specification doesn't matter, since the 4-core option says that you're getting 16GB.)

From the webpage https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-github-codespaces-clients:
"If you encounter issues using GitHub Codespaces in a browser that is not Chromium-based, try switching to a Chromium-based browser, such as Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge."
If something works in Chrome but not other browsers then Chrome is the issue.

Patrick Massot said:

If something works in Chrome but not other browsers then Chrome is the issue.

I would blame the website actually

Codespaces IME (which is limited) works fine in Firefox, but if you have all the security settings turned up (which you should) then it requires adding an allowlist entry for the actual codespace URL (i.e. the one that is specific to the codespace that gets spun up) otherwise it will not be able to connect. Last I recall, this is documented nowhere!

Anatole Dedecker said:

I would blame the website actually

Safari is the Internet Explorer of our time, no website should be blamed for it.
(Firefox is also heading there since Mozilla cut their team & funding)
This is getting really off-topic so we should stop, but you may want to read https://denodell.com/blog/browsers-treat-big-sites-differently for instance.
